analysis.title: Bessent's Pop Quiz: Citi Says Dealer Questions Confirm 20Y, 30Y Auction Cuts Are Coming
key_insights: Treasury's dealer questionnaire for the November refunding asked about long-end buyback effects and about what future auction size changes to consider. Citi (Jason Williams, 'Chips and the dip') reads this as support for its call that Treasury cuts 20Y and 30Y auction sizes by $3bn each on November 4.

The cut would leave 20Y new issues at $13bn (reopenings $10bn) and 30Y new issues at $22bn (reopenings $19bn). That is about $6bn less supply per month, roughly $72bn a year if the cuts last a full year.

Citi argues Treasury raised the long-end buyback caps to limit the long-end selloff rather than for market functioning. Over the past year 30Y auctions stopped through the when-issued level by 0.23bp on average, and 20Y auctions tailed by 0.02bp. The first two operations under the $6bn cap were not maxed out.

30Y yields are more than 20bps higher than when the buyback cap increase was announced and 60bps higher year to date. The first two operations under the new $6bn cap took $5.19bn and $4.08bn. The three since then were maxed out, with $46.4bn of offers on Oct 1 in the 10Y-20Y bucket, $40.8bn more on Thursday, and $14.9bn of offers for $6bn accepted on Oct 8 in the 20Y-30Y bucket.

Citi expects the selloff in long-end yields and the weak early buyback results to push Treasury to shift long-end issuance into T-bills. September's 20Y auction priced with a large tail and the lowest foreign demand on record.

Market positioning already reflects the expected cut. The 20Y has outperformed the 10Y and 30Y on the 10s20s30s fly, and Citi's preferred 10s20s swap spread steepener is at the upper end of its range, at -20bps as of noon Friday. Citi keeps TIPS sizes unchanged.
Citi expects $594bn of private borrowing needs in Q4-26 and $556bn in Q1-27, with a TGA target of $850bn to $950bn. Financing estimates are due Monday Nov 2 at 3pm.

Citi expects bill auction sizes to be trimmed in late October or early November, cut again in December, and guided higher across the curve by mid-January. Bills are projected at 24.4% of marketable debt by end-2027, versus 21.6% at end-2025, with the debt ceiling assumed to bind in H1-2027.

Wednesday's hotter-than-expected CPI first pushed the 2Y up as much as 16bps in a bear flattener. The move reversed as risk assets sold off, and the 10Y and 30Y ended the day in a bull flattener. Citi calls this a partial reversal of the AI-driven real yield sell-off from the prior month, and the 30Y real yield and Nasdaq 100 have moved up together all year.

Goldman Prime's 'AI Unwinds' note says hedge funds net sold global AI stocks for five straight sessions, reversing all cumulative net buying since the start of 2025. The article ties hyperscaler bond issuance and Treasuries to the same duration buyers.

Citi stays tactically neutral on duration because rates flip between AI slowdown concerns and rising energy costs. It is receiving October OIS, expects a Fed pause in October and a hike in December, and the market prices a 15% chance of an October hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Citi expects a $3bn cut to 20Y and 30Y auctions, supported by the questionnaire, which would ease long-end supply and support the 20Y and the swap spread steepener.
tension_points.bear_case: Cutting supply creates no new buyers and pushes the problem into the bill market as the debt ceiling nears. The article says Citi's $3bn may be too conservative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Treasury announces no cut to 20Y and 30Y auction sizes at the November 4 refunding at 8:30am ET.

theme_stances.evidence: these questions support our view that on November 4th Treasury will reduce bond auction sizes
